name: Mental Maths: 2-Digit × 2-Digit — Near Bases & Difference of Squares
description: KaTeX-enabled advanced multiplication practice for products near 10, 50, and 100; balanced products; and the same-tens-units-sum-to-10 pattern. It teaches conditions, padding, carry handling, limits, errors, and method selection.
estimatedTime: 170–220 minutes for a first focused pass; then 10–20 minute review bursts

cards.term: Near Bases & Difference of Squares: When is near-base multiplication useful?
cards.definition:
When both numbers are close to the same base, usually 10, 50, or 100.

$$
\begin{aligned}
97\times96 \\
&=93|12 \\
&=9312
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Near Bases & Difference of Squares: How does below-100 multiplication work?
cards.definition:
Cross-subtract for the left part; multiply deficits for the right part.

$$
\begin{aligned}
97\times94 \\
97-6&=91 \\
3\times6&=18 \\
97\times94&=9118
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Near Bases & Difference of Squares: Why does the right part need two digits near 100?
cards.definition: Because it represents the remainder out of 100. 98 × 97 = 95|06 = 9506, not 956.

cards.term: Near Bases & Difference of Squares: What if the right part is 100 or more?
cards.definition:
Carry into the left part.

$$
\begin{aligned}
88\times87 \\
75|156&=76|56 \\
&=7656
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Near Bases & Difference of Squares: How does above-100 multiplication work?
cards.definition:
Cross-add for the left part; multiply surpluses for the right part.

$$
\begin{aligned}
103\times107 \\
103+7&=110 \\
3\times7&=21 \\
103\times107&=11021
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Near Bases & Difference of Squares: What is the difference-of-squares identity?
Near Bases & Difference of Squares: When is a midpoint of 50 useful?
cards.definition:
When the factors are equally spaced around 50.

$$
\begin{aligned}
46\times54 \\
&=50^2-4^2 \\
&=2484
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Near Bases & Difference of Squares: What is the same-tens, units-sum-to-10 pattern?
cards.definition: For 43 × 47: 4 × 5 = 20 and 3 × 7 = 21, so 2021. It works only when tens match and units sum to 10.

cards.term: Near Bases & Difference of Squares: Which method is best for 97 × 94?
cards.definition:
Near-100 below-base method.

$$
\begin{aligned}
97-6&=91 \\
3\times6&=18 \\
97\times94&=9118
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Near Bases & Difference of Squares: Which method is best for 103 × 97?
cards.definition:
Difference of squares around 100.

$$
\begin{aligned}
103\times97 \\
&=100^2-3^2 \\
&=9991
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Near Bases & Difference of Squares: Which method is best for 43 × 47?
cards.definition:
Same-tens, units-sum-to-10 pattern.

$$
\begin{aligned}
4\times5&=20 \\
3\times7&=21 \\
43\times47&=2021
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Near Bases & Difference of Squares: When should you not use these methods?
cards.definition: When the numbers do not fit the conditions. For 43 × 27, use core splitting instead.
